Verdict: ACCEPTThe new ceiling-descent theorem is valid under its stated full-source decomposition, endpoint-disjointness, confinement, and retained-support completeness hypotheses. The geometric conclusions hold for all four horizontal types initially allowed, arbitrary even horizontal widths and transverse depths, and every standard rotor orientation. The exact peeling identity follows when the surviving horizontal projections start at even columns.The decisive step is sound: completeness forces an actual consuming source, its entire connected endpoint graph is confined to the stated five-row rectangle, and its corner position forces another north source with a strictly smaller left endpoint. The lower bound for that coordinate comes from the same fixed V throughout the argument. Boundary exclusion therefore follows without being assumed in the descent. I find no canonical counterexample or substantive proof gap.    six-row-ceiling-descent-audit1. The source classification covers the permitted hypothesesFor the supplied canonical  $U(B,d,f)$ , the endpoint bounding dimensions before transposition are
$$B\ \text{columns},\qquad \max(d,f)+1\ \text{rows}.$$
Here  $B\ge6$  and  $d,f\ge4$  are even.Without transposition, confinement to six rows implies
$$\max(d,f)+1\le6.$$
Evenness then forces  $d=f=4$ . A downward source can have its outer bar on row  $0$  or  $1$ ; an upward source can have it on row  $4$  or  $5$ . These are precisely  $H_0,H_1,H_4,H_5$ . There is no upper bound on  $B$ .After transposition, the vertical span is  $B$ , so  $B=6$ . Its two-column bar fills all six rows, while the two horizontal stem depths remain arbitrary permitted even integers. Thus the classification imposes no artificial bound on transverse depths either.Two elementary separation facts consequently hold before using completeness:Every horizontal source has a full bar on row  $1$  or  $4$ , and both side columns contain every row from  $1$  through  $4$ . If two projections overlapped, the later left side would meet the earlier source’s full interior bar. Hence horizontal projections are pairwise disjoint.A V bar fills all six rows in each of its two columns. Neither bar column can lie in a horizontal projection, because it would meet that horizontal source’s full bar.These arguments permit all four horizontal phases and arbitrary column parity.The needed north-source data also follow directly from the canonical support formula. For either  $H_0$  or  $H_4$ , with projection  $[L,R]$ ,
$$(0,L),(4,L)\in E_H,\qquad
(4,L-1)\in S_H,$$
and its entire left side on rows  $0,\ldots,4$  consists of endpoints. The support at  $(4,L-1)$  has different canonical roles in the two phases, but it is an original support in both.2. Completeness forces a consumer inside the actual rectangleFix a right-facing V with bar columns  $b,b+1$ , top depth  $f$ , and bottom depth  $d$ . Its top and bottom stem intervals beyond the bar are
$$\{0\}\times[b+2,b+f],
\qquad
\{5\}\times[b+2,b+d].$$
Suppose its bottom stem enters a north source  $A$ , meaning  $H_0$  or  $H_4$ , from the left. If  $L$  is that source’s left endpoint, then
$$b+2\le L\le b+d.$$
Since  $A$  owns  $(0,L)$ , disjointness from the top stem implies
$$b+f<L.$$
In particular,
$$L\ge b+f+1\ge b+5. \tag{3}$$
Now consider the original support
$$s=(4,L-1)\in S_A.$$
It has the two distinct occupied neighbours
$$(4,L)\in E_A,
\qquad
(5,L-1)\in E_V.$$
The second membership follows from (3) and the bottom-stem reach. Also: $s\notin E_A$ , because its column precedes  $A$ ’s projection. $s\notin E_V$ , because the only V endpoints on row  $4$  are in its bar columns, whereas  $L-1\ge b+4$ . $s$  lies inside the pocket and cannot be an old boundary endpoint.If  $s$  were unconsumed, the support-retention hypothesis would leave it occupied, and completeness would require its occupied degree to equal one. Its two displayed occupied neighbours contradict that requirement. Therefore an actual third source  $C$  owns  $s$ .This is the correct use of completeness. It produces an endpoint in the given configuration; it does not merely identify a source that could hypothetically consume the support.The confinement claim holds for the whole consumerThe actual consumer satisfies
$$E_C\subseteq Q,
\qquad
Q=[0,4]\times[b+2,L-1]. \tag{4}$$
To see this, take any nearest-neighbour endpoint path of  $C$  starting at  $s$ . A first exit from  $Q$  would have to cross one of the following boundaries:Exit directionObstructionAbove row  $0$ All new endpoints are confined to rows  $0,\ldots,5$ .Left through column  $b+1$ V occupies that column in every row of the strip.Right through column  $L$  $A$  occupies that column on rows  $0,\ldots,4$ .Below through row  $5$ , between the two wallsV occupies every such point in its bottom stem.Endpoint-disjointness forbids crossing the occupied boundaries. The right wall is also completed at  $(5,L)$  by V.Because  $C$ ’s endpoint graph is connected, every endpoint of  $C$  is reachable by such a path. Thus the argument confines the entire source, including a source whose allowed width or depth was initially arbitrarily large.No support wall is being substituted for an endpoint wall here. The blockers used in (4) are actual endpoints of  $A$  and V, together with the global endpoint confinement to the strip.3. Corner reception forces a bounded integer descentThe point  $s=(4,L-1)$  is the southeast corner of  $Q$ . A full source contained in this rectangle and owning that corner must be another north source.The classification is exhaustive:A transverse U cannot fit. It requires six rows.A horizontal U must have both depths  $4$ . It therefore spans five rows. Since it is contained in rows  $0,\ldots,4$  and reaches row  $4$ , its outer bar is on row  $0$  or  $4$ . It is  $H_0$  or  $H_4$ .A rotor cannot own this corner. The two normalized rotor shapes cover all eight dihedral images, and neither contains the southeast corner of its bounding rectangle. If a rotor were contained in  $Q$  and owned  $s$ , that point would attain both its maximal row and maximal column, contradicting this shape identity.For the resulting north source  $C$ , its right endpoint is exactly  $L-1$ . If its left endpoint is  $L'$  and its width is  $B_C\ge6$ , then
$$L'=L-B_C\le L-6.$$
Confinement also gives
$$b+2\le L'.$$
Thus
$$b+2\le L'\le L-6. \tag{5}$$
The same fixed V bottom stem reaches  $L'$ , since
$$L'\le L\le b+d.$$
Disjointness from the same fixed V top stem gives the renewed lower bound
$$L'\ge b+f+1.$$
The source  $C$  has its own original support  $(4,L'-1)$ , so the forcing and confinement argument applies again.The contradiction can be stated without choosing an infinite sequence. For this fixed V, let  $D$  be the set of left endpoints of north sources reached from the left by its bottom stem. Under the assumed contact: $D$  is nonempty.Every  $x\in D$  satisfies  $x\ge b+f+1$ .Every  $x\in D$  forces another  $x'\in D$  satisfying  $x'\le x-6$ .A nonempty bounded-below subset of the integers has a least element, which the third property contradicts.Equivalently, the nonnegative integer
$$x-(b+f+1)$$
strictly decreases at every forced step. The bar position  $b$  and top depth  $f$  stay fixed throughout, so the lower bound does not move with the consumer. If a remaining rectangle is too narrow to contain another width-six source, the contradiction occurs at that step.Horizontal reflection proves the corresponding exclusion for a V entering from the right. Since a V bar cannot intersect a horizontal projection, this proves the general statement
$$\boxed{\text{No V bottom endpoint lies over an }H_0\text{ or }H_4\text{ projection.}}$$
This is an unrestricted parameter proof. Its validity does not depend on the largest width used in a checker.4. Boundary exclusion is noncircularThe preceding descent argument allowed  $H_0$  throughout. In particular, a forced receiver was allowed to be either  $H_0$  or  $H_4$ . No boundary exclusion has been used to obtain the north-source lemma.Now suppose an  $H_0$  exists, with left endpoint  $L$ . Its original support
$$t=(5,L)$$
has the two occupied neighbours
$$(4,L)\in E_{H_0},
\qquad
(6,L)\in E_{\mathrm{old}}.$$
Completeness forces an actual endpoint at  $t$ .Every permitted non-V owner is excluded:Possible owner of  $t$ Reason it cannot own  $t$  $H_0$  or  $H_4$ These types have no endpoints on row  $5$ . $H_1$ Its row- $5$  endpoint has a same-column leg endpoint on row  $4$ , colliding with the original  $H_0$ . $H_5$ Its full inner bar supplies the same-column endpoint on row  $4$ , again colliding.RotorA rotor confined to the strip and reaching row  $5$  reaches it at its bottom tip; both normalized shapes have an endpoint immediately above that tip.The owner would therefore have to be V. Its bar cannot meet the horizontal projection, and its bottom stem is excluded by the already established north-source lemma. This rules out  $H_0$ .Reflection
$$r\longmapsto 5-r$$
preserves the strip, its occupied old boundary, the canonical source class, endpoint-disjointness, and support completeness. It maps  $H_0$  to  $H_5$ , so  $H_5$  is also absent. It simultaneously maps the bottom-stem exclusion over  $H_4$  to top-stem exclusion over  $H_1$ .For the remaining V endpoints:Over  $H_1$ , a bottom stem entering from either side must pass through  $(5,L)$  or  $(5,R)$ , which are already H endpoints.Over  $H_4$ , the analogous argument excludes top stems using  $(0,L)$  and  $(0,R)$ .V bars were excluded from every horizontal projection at the outset.Consequently,
$$\boxed{\text{No V endpoint occurs anywhere over an interior H projection.}}$$
The logical order is therefore correct: the descent is proved with boundary phases permitted, and is then used to exclude those phases.5. Rotor separation covers every allowed rotor shapeConsider  $H_1$ , with projection  $I=[L,R]$ . Its endpoint set contains the full rows  $1,2$  over  $I$ , and both side columns from row  $1$  through row  $5$ .A rotor endpoint over  $I$  has three possible row locations:Row  $0$ . Since the rotor is confined to the strip, this is a topmost endpoint. In either normalized rotor shape, it has a rotor endpoint immediately below it. That endpoint would collide with the row- $1$  H bar.Rows  $1$  or  $2$ . It directly collides with an H bar.Rows  $3,\ldots,5$ . It must lie strictly between the two H side columns.In the third case, the rotor’s connected endpoint graph is confined to
$$[3,5]\times[L+1,R-1].$$
Its upper exit is blocked by the row- $2$  bar, its side exits by the H side columns, and its lower exit by the strip boundary. This confines the whole rotor, not merely the endpoint initially found over  $I$ .That rectangle has only three rows, whereas every allowed rotor has four-row span. Hence this case is impossible as well.Reflection proves the statement for  $H_4$ . Combining rotor separation with V separation and the previously established disjointness of horizontal projections gives
$$\boxed{
E_C\cap\bigl([0,5]\times I_H\bigr)=\varnothing
\quad\text{for every other source }C.
}$$
No alignment assumption has entered this geometric conclusion.6. The exact simultaneous peeling identity followsLet  $\mathcal H$  be all surviving horizontal sources, assume each starts at even  $L_H$ , and let  $\mathcal R$  be the remaining V/rotor family.Because  $B_H$  is even,
$$I_H=[L_H,L_H+B_H-1]$$
is a union of complete physical tile columns. Every tile touched by an H endpoint lies wholly within those columns. The geometric separation theorem therefore implies that every tile containing an H endpoint is exclusive to that source among endpoint owners.This is enough to obtain the exact inventory identities.Canonical H chargeFor an aligned  $H_1$ , put  $t=B/2$ . $$\max(0,-q_H)=B-1,
\qquad
\mathbf 1_{\{q_H>0\}}=0.$$
This calculation uses the packet’s corrected charge  $M-2T+S$  directly.    six-row-ceiling-descent-auditMixed full tiles and labelled events are unchangedA mixed full tile involving H would require a foreign endpoint in a tile touched by H. Tile exclusivity forbids that. Hence

\sum_{H\in\mathcal H}

&\quad+2\bigl(J(\mathcal R\cup\mathcal H)-J(\mathcal R)\bigr)

&=\sum_{H\in\mathcal H}(B_H-1).

Thus

\Phi(\mathrm{full})
=
